summary:
Independent review of Shiji 115 units s0001-s0032, nineteen owned claims, fourteen active-date hints, and people p001-p014. Chinese dating formulas were read first. 燕王盧綰反，入匈奴 converts to BC 195 from Gaozu 12 in Shiji 8/93 and Zizhi Tongjian 高帝十二年（丙午，公元前一九五年）; Wiman's founding is that same named trigger. 孝惠、高后時 is an uncertainty window for the Liaodong-Wiman pact, converted as Hui accession-to-death BC 195-188 plus Lü's power BC 188-180 (高后八年). Numbered-year tables that start Hui 1 at 194 and 高后 1 at 187 are preserved as competing 逾年改元 labels, not as a reason to invent a different event year. 元封二年 / 元封三年夏 equate conventionally to BC 109 / BC 108 (Yuanfeng 前110-前105). Academia Sinica's public converter begins at AD 1 and was not used; Wikipedia's Yuanfeng month table gives Julian-style Western month-days, which are identified as such and are not applied as Gregorian event dates for these year- or season-only labels. Autumn of Yuanfeng 2 and the inherited year-2 campaign block through Wei Shan's execution remain BC 109 as conventional year-labels. No owned unit states a birth, age, or dated death for Wiman or his unnamed son; those omissions stay unresolved. Hints match the owned claims plus read-only 108 context for Ugeo, the emperor, Yang Pu, Xun Zhi, and Changjiang. No posthumous reception is used as a life date. All owned checks are supported; findings are empty.
Owned units s0033–s0064 contain one explicit calendar date, 元封三年夏, and a continuous siege-to-punishment sequence after that summer. Emperor Wu of Han’s Yuanfeng 3 is the conventional Western year 108 BC; because the Qin-Han civil year then began in month 10, winter of Yuanfeng 3 falls in 109 BC, but summer (months 4–6) is in 108 BC, so the summer assassination and all subsequent narrative events may carry westernYear 108. No births or ages appear. Deaths of Gongsun Sui, Lu Ren, Ugeo, Cheng Ji, and Xun Zhi are each already claimed; Yang Pu is sentenced but ransomed, so he correctly has no death. Gongsun Sui’s mission and execution, and Lu Ren’s surrender and death on the road, sit in the undated stretch after the Yuanfeng 2 campaign opening and before summer Yuanfeng 3, so the inclusive 109–108 bounds (onOrAfter 109, onOrBefore 108) are the right shape of uncertainty rather than a dynasty-long activity span. Han Yin and Wang Xia surrender in that same stretch but are also enfeoffed after the summer climax, so a Yuanfeng 3 / 108 attestation is supported. Sima Qian’s 太史公曰 is an undated retrospective remark and correctly has empty active hints. Hints for p015–p021 match the supported personal events and do not treat later reception as living activity.

itemChecks.event: Wiman flees Yan, crosses the Pae, and makes himself king of Joseon after Lu Wan rebels and enters the Xiongnu.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wiman (p001). The chapter dates his exile and self-enthronement only by 燕王盧綰反，入匈奴, not by a Han year. Shiji 8 places the open strike on Lu Wan in 高祖十二年二月 and his flight after 四月甲辰; Shiji 93 likewise has the year-12 revolt and 盧綰遂將其眾亡入匈奴. Zizhi Tongjian labels 高帝十二年 as 公元前一九五年, and conventional tables end Gaozu at BC 195. That is a year-label conversion of the named revolt-and-flight, not a proleptic Gregorian day. Pre-Taichu October year-start means Gaozu 12 begins in BC 196, but 入匈奴 follows the fourth-month death and falls in BC 195. Endpoint 195 is therefore the conventional Western year of Wiman's own founding cluster.

evidence.quote: 燕王盧綰反，入匈奴，滿亡命，聚黨千餘人，魋結蠻夷服而東走出塞，渡浿水，居秦故空地上下鄣，稍役屬真番、朝鮮蠻夷及故燕、齊亡命者王之，都王險。

itemChecks.event: The Liaodong governor binds Wiman as an outer vassal, and the Han court then lets him use that mandate to subdue neighboring towns.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wiman (p001). The pact and the later 上許之 expansion are dated only 孝惠、高后時, a joint period, so the Western span is an uncertainty window for one event, not activity through a dynasty. Start BC 195 is Hui's accession year after Gaozu's death in Gaozu 12; Hui year 1 itself opens in the tenth month of BC 195. End BC 180 is 高后八年, when Lü dies. Competing numbered-year tables start Hui 1 at 194 and 高后 1 at 187; those are 逾年改元 labels, not a second invented endpoint for this undated pact. 天下初定 hints early in the period but does not narrow the source's named window. Sequence holds: founding at Lu Wan's flight, then this Hui-Gao pact.

evidence.quote: 會孝惠、高后時天下初定，遼東太守即約滿為外臣，保塞外蠻夷，無使盜邊；
以聞，上許之，以故滿得兵威財物侵降其旁小邑，真番、臨屯皆來服屬，方數千里。

itemChecks.event: Lu Wan, King of Yan, rebels and flees into Xiongnu territory.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Lu Wan (p002). Chapter 115 states his revolt and 入匈奴 without a year; the Western year is the same Gaozu-12 conversion as claim-5. Shiji 8 has the year-12 attack on Yan and 盧綰聞高祖崩，遂亡入匈奴. Zizhi Tongjian 高帝十二年（丙午，公元前一九五年）. Endpoint 195 dates Lu Wan's own open revolt and flight, not a later quotation. Secret dealings in Gaozu 11 are a different, earlier episode and are not used here.

evidence.quote: 燕王盧綰反，入匈奴

itemChecks.event: Emperor Hui is named as the first reign in the 孝惠、高后時 frame for the Liaodong-Wiman agreement.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Emperor Hui (p003). His only chapter role is the period label 孝惠 (and possibly the unnamed 上 who later approves the pact). The interval BC 195-188 converts 孝惠時 as time on the throne—accession after Gaozu's BC 195 death, death in Hui year 7—not a claim that Hui campaigned in Joseon every year. Competing reading: numbered 孝惠元年-七年 as BC 194-188. Endpoints are reign bounds for that label, not invented life dates.

evidence.quote: 會孝惠、高后時天下初定

itemChecks.event: Empress Dowager Gao is named as the second reign in the 孝惠、高后時 frame for the Liaodong-Wiman agreement.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Empress Dowager Gao (p004). She is a period marker, not an actor in Joseon. Interval BC 188-180 is her power from Hui's death to 高后八年. Competing numbered 高后元年-八年 is BC 187-180. The window is the 高后時 half of the source phrase, not dynasty-long activity.

evidence.quote: 會孝惠、高后時天下初定

itemChecks.event: Kingship passes from Wiman through this unnamed son to grandson Ugeo.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is the unnamed son (p005). 傳子至孫右渠 attests a succession link and gives no year, age, birth, or death. undatedSourceAttestation with unresolved hint is required: the son could have ruled at any time after Wiman's Hui-Gao activity and before Ugeo's Yuanfeng 2 refusal. Inventing bounds from those neighboring dates would fabricate endpoints. 同生 is not in the passage.

evidence.quote: 傳子至孫右渠

itemChecks.event: Ugeo refuses She He's edict and then resists the Han armies sent against him.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Ugeo (p006). s0011 dates the rebuke 元封二年; s0018 and s0021 continue the same undated campaign block before 元封三年夏. Conventional equation Yuanfeng 2 = BC 109 (Yuanfeng 前110-前105). This is a reign-year label, not a Gregorian day; October year-start puts the first months of Yuanfeng 2 in BC 110, but the chapter gives no month for the edict. Later killing in 元封三年夏 is a separate event and does not move this year-2 attestation. Endpoint 109 is the conventional Western year of Ugeo's own year-2 resistance.

evidence.quote: 元封二年，漢使涉何譙諭右渠，終不肯奉詔。
右渠發兵距險。

itemChecks.event: The Son of Heaven sends She He, then raises convicts and dispatches generals against Joseon.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is the Han emperor (p007), named only as 天子. s0011-s0016 sit under 元封二年, with 其秋 marking the autumn sailing. Conventional Yuanfeng 2 = BC 109. Autumn of that year falls in BC 109 even on the October-year calendar. Context Yuanfeng 3 / 108 is a later event, not this dispatch. Endpoint 109 dates his own year-2 orders.

evidence.quote: 元封二年，漢使涉何譙諭右渠，終不肯奉詔。
其秋，遣樓船將軍楊仆從齊浮渤海；

itemChecks.event: She He rebukes Ugeo, has Chang stabbed at the Pae, and is then appointed eastern Liaodong commandant.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is She He (p008). The mission opens 元封二年 and the killing, report, and appointment follow in the same block before 其秋. Conventional year BC 109. These are She He's own acts, not a later commemoration. Endpoint 109 is the year-label of that mission.

evidence.quote: 元封二年，漢使涉何譙諭右渠，終不肯奉詔。
何去至界上，臨浿水，使御刺殺送何者朝鮮裨王長，即渡，馳入塞，遂歸報天子曰「殺朝鮮將」。

itemChecks.event: Joseon troops attack and kill She He after his appointment in Liaodong.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is She He (p008). 朝鮮怨何，發兵襲攻殺何 is his death, still before 其秋 and the 天子募罪人 levy, so it remains under the 元封二年 heading. Conventional BC 109. Endpoint 109 dates the killing itself, not a posthumous reference.

evidence.quote: 朝鮮怨何，發兵襲攻殺何。

itemChecks.event: Joseon deputy king Chang escorts She He to the Pae River frontier.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Chang (p009). He appears only as the escort killed in the 元封二年 She He narrative, immediately after s0011's year heading. Conventional BC 109. Endpoint 109 is Chang's own escort/death episode, not Ugeo's later war.

evidence.quote: 元封二年，漢使涉何譙諭右渠，終不肯奉詔。
使御刺殺送何者朝鮮裨王長

itemChecks.event: She He's driver stabs Joseon deputy king Chang at the Pae River.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Chang (p009). The stabbing is explicit in s0012 in the same 元封二年 block as She He's mission. Conventional BC 109. This is Chang's death, not a later honor. Endpoint 109.

evidence.quote: 使御刺殺送何者朝鮮裨王長

itemChecks.event: Yang Pu sails from Qi, reaches Wanggeom first, is defeated, and hides in the mountains.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Yang Pu (p010). 其秋 names the dispatch; s0020-s0022 continue that autumn campaign under 元封二年. Conventional Yuanfeng 2 autumn = BC 109. Context Yuanfeng 3 is the later siege/punishment year and does not redate this first arrival. Endpoint 109 is Yang Pu's own year-2 operations.

evidence.quote: 其秋，遣樓船將軍楊仆從齊浮渤海；
樓船將軍將齊兵七千人先至王險。

itemChecks.event: Xun Zhi marches from Liaodong against Ugeo and fights west of the Pae.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Xun Zhi (p011). He is paired with the 其秋 levy and fights in s0019/s0023 still before the Yuanfeng 3 summer marker. Conventional BC 109. His marketplace execution is a later Yuanfeng 3 event and must not be folded into this year-2 attestation. Endpoint 109 dates his own first-year command.

evidence.quote: 兵五萬人，左將軍荀彘出遼東：討右渠。
左將軍擊朝鮮浿水西軍，未能破自前。

itemChecks.event: Battalion commander Duo leads the Liaodong troops in an early charge that collapses.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Duo (p012). s0019 follows the 其秋 dispatch of the Left General's column. Conventional autumn of Yuanfeng 2 = BC 109. Endpoint 109 is Duo's own sortie, immediately before his execution in the same sentence.

evidence.quote: 其秋，遣樓船將軍楊仆從齊浮渤海；
左將軍卒正多率遼東兵先縱，敗散，多還走，坐法斬。

itemChecks.event: Duo is executed under military law after the Liaodong troops flee.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Duo (p012). 坐法斬 is in the same autumn action as the failed charge. Source date 元封二年其秋 is more precise than the year heading alone; Western year 109 matches autumn months of Yuanfeng 2 on the October-year calendar. Season is not a month/day, so no proleptic-Gregorian day is claimed. Endpoint 109 is Duo's death year.

evidence.quote: 左將軍卒正多率遼東兵先縱，敗散，多還走，坐法斬。

itemChecks.event: Wei Shan is sent to persuade Ugeo after both Han generals have failed.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wei Shan (p013). He first appears after the autumn failures, still in the annalistic block that opened 元封二年 and before 元封三年夏. The chapter presents this embassy as a year-2 sequel, not as an undated gap requiring unresolved:true. Conventional label BC 109. A winter/spring slip into Yuanfeng 3 could still be late BC 109 on the October calendar; the source does not give a month, so the year-label 109 is the supported conversion rather than a fabricated day. Endpoint 109 dates Wei Shan's own embassy.

evidence.quote: 元封二年，漢使涉何譙諭右渠，終不肯奉詔。
天子為兩將未有利，乃使衛山因兵威往諭右渠。

itemChecks.event: The Son of Heaven executes Wei Shan after the failed surrender talks.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wei Shan (p013). 天子誅山 has no new year; it closes the embassy that sits after 其秋 and before the multi-month siege that 元封三年夏 then dates. Annalistic grammar keeps it under 元封二年. Conventional BC 109. This is Wei Shan's death, not a posthumous honor. Certainty explicit-event-contextual-date matches inherited year-heading dating. Endpoint 109.

evidence.quote: 山還報天子，天子誅山。

itemChecks.event: Ugeo sends the crown prince with arms and gifts to apologize; the prince refuses to cross the Pae and turns back.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Changjiang (p014), identified in this extraction as the 太子 of s0027-s0029. That failed crossing belongs to the Wei Shan embassy under the 元封二年 heading. Conventional BC 109. The later Yuanfeng 3 surrender/enfeoffment is a later event of the same man and correctly stays off this row. Endpoint 109 dates the prince's own aborted crossing.

evidence.quote: 遣太子入謝，獻馬五千匹，及饋軍糧。
太子亦疑使者左將軍詐殺之，遂不渡浿水，復引歸。

itemChecks.event: Wiman founds Joseon at Lu Wan's revolt and later accepts the Hui-Gao outer-vassal pact.
itemChecks.reason: Hints BC 195 and BC 195-180 match Wiman's two dated chapter events: founding at Lu Wan's flight and the undated pact inside 孝惠、高后時. They are not a lifespan and do not use the later Ugeo war as Wiman's activity. No birth, death, or age is in the owned units; 傳子至孫 implies succession without a year, so no death hint is required.

evidence.quote: 燕王盧綰反，入匈奴，滿亡命
會孝惠、高后時天下初定，遼東太守即約滿為外臣

itemChecks.event: Lu Wan rebels as King of Yan and flees to the Xiongnu.
itemChecks.reason: Hint BC 195 matches Lu Wan's only chapter event. The chapter does not date his later death among the Xiongnu; that absence is correct and is not filled from another biography.

evidence.quote: 燕王盧綰反，入匈奴

itemChecks.event: Emperor Hui is the first reign named in 孝惠、高后時 for the Liaodong-Wiman pact.
itemChecks.reason: Hint BC 195-188 tracks claim-21's conversion of 孝惠時 to accession-death years, not a Joseon campaign by Hui. It does not borrow Gao hou's 180 endpoint.

evidence.quote: 會孝惠、高后時天下初定

itemChecks.event: Empress Dowager Gao is the second reign named in 孝惠、高后時 for the Liaodong-Wiman pact.
itemChecks.reason: Hint BC 188-180 tracks claim-26's conversion of 高后時 to her years of power. It is not Lü's biography imported as Joseon activity.

evidence.quote: 會孝惠、高后時天下初定

itemChecks.event: The unnamed son is only a succession link between Wiman and Ugeo; the hint correctly states that this person lacks a dated event of his own.
itemChecks.reason: unresolved is required. s0009 names no year for the son's reign, birth, death, or age. Bounding him by Wiman's last dated year and Ugeo's 109 would invent endpoints.

evidence.quote: 傳子至孫右渠

itemChecks.event: Ugeo refuses the Yuanfeng 2 edict and is later killed in Yuanfeng 3 summer.
itemChecks.reason: BC 109 matches owned claim-35; BC 108 matches read-only context 元封三年夏…殺朝鮮王右渠. The death is Ugeo's own event and is kept off the year-2 row. Hints do not turn the 108 killing into a 109 life date.

evidence.quote: 元封二年，漢使涉何譙諭右渠，終不肯奉詔。
元封三年夏，尼谿相參乃使人殺朝鮮王右渠來降。

itemChecks.event: The Son of Heaven opens the Joseon war in Yuanfeng 2 and the campaign continues in Yuanfeng 3.
itemChecks.reason: BC 109 matches owned claim-51; BC 108 matches context Yuanfeng 3. Both are his own wartime orders, not posthumous honors.

evidence.quote: 元封二年，漢使涉何譙諭右渠，終不肯奉詔。
天子募罪人擊朝鮮。

itemChecks.event: She He goes as envoy in Yuanfeng 2 and is killed the same year before the autumn levy.
itemChecks.reason: Hint BC 109 matches claim-61 and death claim-66. No 108 hint is warranted: he is already dead when 其秋 armies move.

evidence.quote: 元封二年，漢使涉何譙諭右渠
朝鮮怨何，發兵襲攻殺何。

itemChecks.event: Deputy king Chang is stabbed at the Pae while escorting She He in Yuanfeng 2.
itemChecks.reason: Hint BC 109 matches claim-70 and claim-71. Chang does not appear in the Yuanfeng 3 block, so no 108 hint.

evidence.quote: 使御刺殺送何者朝鮮裨王長

itemChecks.event: Yang Pu commands the tower-ship force in Yuanfeng 2 and is still in the field in Yuanfeng 3.
itemChecks.reason: BC 109 matches owned claim-76; BC 108 matches context year-3 activity. The later demotion is his own Yuanfeng 3 legal event, not a posthumous notice, and it belongs on the 108 hint rather than the 109 row.

evidence.quote: 其秋，遣樓船將軍楊仆從齊浮渤海；
樓船亦往會，居城南。

itemChecks.event: Xun Zhi commands the land army in Yuanfeng 2 and is executed after the Yuanfeng 3 settlement.
itemChecks.reason: BC 109 matches owned claim-91; BC 108 matches context attestation and death. The marketplace execution is Xun Zhi's own death in the later year and is not fed back as a 109 life date.

evidence.quote: 左將軍荀彘出遼東：討右渠。
左將軍徵至，坐爭功相嫉，乖計，棄市。

itemChecks.event: Duo's failed charge and military-law execution occur in autumn of Yuanfeng 2.
itemChecks.reason: Hint BC 109 matches claim-107 and death claim-111 (元封二年其秋). He does not survive into the Yuanfeng 3 narrative.

evidence.quote: 左將軍卒正多率遼東兵先縱，敗散，多還走，坐法斬。

itemChecks.event: Wei Shan negotiates with Ugeo and is then executed, both under the Yuanfeng 2 campaign heading.
itemChecks.reason: Hint BC 109 matches claim-115 and death claim-118. No 108 hint is required: the chapter does not move 天子誅山 under 元封三年夏. A possible year-boundary reading is preserved in the claim-118 reason and is not turned into a second exact year.

evidence.quote: 乃使衛山因兵威往諭右渠。
山還報天子，天子誅山。

itemChecks.event: The crown prince turns back at the Pae in Yuanfeng 2 and later helps settle Joseon in Yuanfeng 3.
itemChecks.reason: BC 109 matches owned claim-123; BC 108 matches context 長降 in the settlement/enfeoffment. The later enfeoffment is his own Yuanfeng 3 act, not a posthumous commemoration, and stays off the 109 row.

evidence.quote: 遣太子入謝，獻馬五千匹，及饋軍糧。
太子亦疑使者左將軍詐殺之，遂不渡浿水，復引歸。

itemChecks.event: Ugeo is named as the living king of Joseon at the moment Shen has him killed in summer Yuanfeng 3.
itemChecks.reason: The dated event belongs to Ugeo (p006): s0052 names 朝鮮王右渠 as the victim of the summer assassination, which attests him on that date rather than a descendant’s later act. The sole explicit endpoint is 元封三年夏 in the same sentence. Han Emperor Wu, Yuanfeng era year 3, is the conventional Western year 108 BC; 夏 corresponds to lunar months 4–6, which the verified 元封 luni-solar table places in 108 BC (April–June), after the Han year had opened in month 10 of 109 BC. A year-precision westernYear 108 is therefore justified for this seasonal date and does not require a second invented endpoint.

evidence.quote: 元封三年夏，尼谿相參乃使人殺朝鮮王右渠來降。

itemChecks.event: Ugeo is assassinated by men sent by Shen, the Chancellor of Nixi.
itemChecks.reason: The death belongs to Ugeo (p006), not to Shen’s later enfeoffment or to any commemorative retelling. s0052 states 使人殺朝鮮王右渠 with authorityPerson Shen (尼谿相參). The date is the same explicit 元封三年夏; westernYear 108 BC is the Gregorian year of that summer under Emperor Wu’s Yuanfeng 3, as justified for claim-36. Certainty explicit is earned because the death and the Chinese date stand in one sentence.

evidence.quote: 尼谿相參乃使人殺朝鮮王右渠來降。

itemChecks.event: Emperor Wu recalls the Left General after the Yuanfeng 3 Joseon settlement and has him executed.
itemChecks.reason: The dated event is Emperor Wu’s (p007) imperial recall and marketplace execution of Xun Zhi, which follows the summer climax without a new year label. s0052 supplies 元封三年; s0057’s 徵至 and 棄市 are court punishments that only the reigning 天子 issues in this chapter. Because the act is after 元封三年夏, it falls in the later months of Yuanfeng 3, all in 108 BC, so the conventional year-only westernYear 108 is not a New-Year edge case. The year is contextual rather than restated in s0057, matching explicit-event-contextual-date. No later quotation is being back-dated as living activity.

evidence.quote: 元封三年夏，尼谿相參乃使人殺朝鮮王右渠來降。
左將軍徵至，坐爭功相嫉，乖計，棄市。

itemChecks.event: Yang Pu, the General of the Tower Ships, is convicted after the campaign and ransomed to commoner status.
itemChecks.reason: The event belongs to Yang Pu (p010): s0058 judges 樓船將軍 for the Liekou unauthorized attack and records 贖為庶人, which is his own punishment, not a death. The year is carried from 元封三年 in s0052 through the unbroken aftermath (pacification, enfeoffments, then the two generals’ sentences). That aftermath is after summer, hence Western 108 BC. 當誅 marks a sentence, not an execution, so omitting a death claim is required.

evidence.quote: 元封三年夏
樓船將軍亦坐兵至洌口，當待左將軍，擅先縱，失亡多，當誅，贖為庶人。

itemChecks.event: Xun Zhi, the Left General, finishes the Yuanfeng 3 pacification of Joseon and is then recalled for punishment.
itemChecks.reason: The attestation belongs to Xun Zhi (p011). After 元封三年夏 he has Changjiang and Zui proclaim to the people, executes Cheng Ji, and is himself 徵至 (s0054, s0057). Those are his own command and recall, dated by narrative continuity from s0052’s Yuanfeng 3, not by a descendant’s act. Western 108 BC follows because the actions stand after summer of that regnal year.

evidence.quote: 元封三年夏，尼谿相參乃使人殺朝鮮王右渠來降。
左將軍使右渠子長降、相路人之子最告諭其民，誅成巳，以故遂定朝鮮，為四郡。
左將軍徵至，坐爭功相嫉，乖計，棄市。

itemChecks.event: Xun Zhi is publicly executed in the marketplace after being recalled to the capital.
itemChecks.reason: The death belongs to Xun Zhi (p011): s0057’s 棄市 is his execution, later recapped in s0063 as 荀彘爭勞，與遂皆誅, which is reception of the same death and must not supply a second life date. The Chinese year is not restated in s0057; it is the continuing Yuanfeng 3 of s0052. Because recall and execution are narrated immediately after the summer pacification and enfeoffments, the endpoint is Yuanfeng 3 / conventional 108 BC, not an open later reign. A year-precision westernYear is justified; a month-day Gregorian date is not claimed.

evidence.quote: 元封三年夏
左將軍徵至，坐爭功相嫉，乖計，棄市。
荀彘爭勞，與遂皆誅。

itemChecks.event: Changjiang, Ugeo’s son, surrenders, helps pacify Joseon, and is enfeoffed as Marquis of Ji.
itemChecks.reason: The attestation belongs to Changjiang (p014): after Ugeo’s summer death, 右渠子長降 is used to instruct the people and 長［降］為幾侯. references.quote: 元封（前110年—前104年四月）是汉武帝的第六个年号。
references.reason: Primary conversion check for ruler, polity, and era: Western Han Emperor Wu, era 元封, year 3 conventionally 108 BC. The same page’s 紀年農曆對照表 states that Qin-Han years then began in lunar month 10 and lists Yuanfeng 3 month 10 as 109 BC 11/10 and months 4–6 as 108 BC 4/7–6/5, so 元封三年夏 is 108 BC while a year-only 元封三年 label must not be treated as a precise Gregorian day.

references.title: 元封
references.quote: 秦漢以夏曆十月為歲首，但月份名稱不變
references.reason: Confirms the civil-year setting used in the conversion: Xia-month names with month 10 as 歲首 before the Taichu reform, which is why winter of Yuanfeng 3 can fall in 109 BC even though the conventional Western year of 元封三年 is 108 BC. Academia Sinica’s public converter range begins at AD 1, so it was not used for this BC date.
